exercises.name: Arc 10
exercises.description: A great endurance exercise to keep you moving for extended periods.
howTo: Perform continuous, low-intensity climbing for 10 minutes on easy terrain, focusing on smooth, controlled movements. This helps build endurance without straining muscles.

exercises.name: 1 on 1 off active
exercises.description: Alternating between activity and rest helps maintain balance and stamina.
howTo: Alternate between one minute of climbing and one minute of rest. During the active phase, climb steadily, and use the rest phase to recover while staying active with light movements.

exercises.description: This training method splits your efforts equally for better results.
howTo: Climb for 50% of your maximum intensity for an extended period, then rest for an equal amount of time. This alternating pattern trains both endurance and power recovery.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: 7:3s
exercises.description: Focus on short bursts of effort with this high-intensity drill.
howTo: Hang on a fingerboard for 7 seconds, then rest for 3 seconds. Repeat for several cycles. This helps build finger strength and endurance for short, intense holds.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Aero 4's
exercises.description: Aerobic endurance is built over time with consistent pacing in this exercise.
howTo: Climb for 4 minutes at a low intensity without stopping. Rest for 4 minutes, then repeat. Focus on maintaining a steady pace to improve aerobic capacity.

exercises.name: Latissimus Dorsi Stretch
exercises.description: A stretch focused on increasing flexibility and range of motion in the back.
howTo: Kneel on the floor and extend your arms forward, palms down. Slowly press your chest toward the ground, stretching the sides of your back. Hold for 30 seconds, then relax.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Relieves tension in the hips and improves posture.
howTo: Step one leg forward into a lunge position, keeping your back leg straight. Push your hips forward to stretch the hip flexor of the back leg. Hold for 30 seconds on each side.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Glute Stretch / Pigeon Pose
exercises.description: A deep stretch that targets the glutes, helping in mobility.
howTo: From a kneeling position, bring one leg forward with the knee bent and the other leg extended behind you. Lower your hips toward the floor to stretch the glute and hip muscles. Hold for 30 seconds.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: An essential stretch for preventing injury in the legs.
howTo: Stand and bend forward at the waist, reaching toward your toes. Keep your legs straight but not locked. Hold for 30 seconds to stretch the hamstrings, then slowly return to standing.

exercises.name: Run
exercises.description: Running builds both physical endurance and mental resilience.
howTo: Start with a warm-up walk or light jog. Increase speed gradually, maintaining a steady pace for the duration of the run. Cool down by walking or jogging at a slower pace.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: MS RPE
exercises.description: A method for assessing workout intensity based on perceived exertion.
howTo: Perform an exercise while monitoring your level of exertion on a scale of 1-10, with 10 being the most intense. Adjust intensity according to the desired difficulty level.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Strength Intervals / 5x3s
exercises.description: Strength is built with high-effort intervals and shorter rest periods.
howTo: Perform 5 sets of 3 intense climbing moves or hangs, with short rest periods in between. Focus on maximal effort during each set to build power and strength.

exercises.name: Board climbing - Max efforts
exercises.description: Push yourself to the limit with maximum effort climbs on the board.
howTo: Climb on a training board using difficult holds or sequences. Perform short, intense sessions focused on maximal effort with longer rest periods to allow full recovery between attempts.

exercises.name: Boulder Pyramid
exercises.description: A structured climbing sequence that helps with strength and technique.
howTo: Climb increasingly difficult boulders in a pyramid sequence (e.g., easy, medium, hard, medium, easy). This method builds both strength and technique as you vary difficulty and intensity.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: An exercise where you hold your body straight and parallel to the floor while resting on your toes and elbows.
howTo: From lying face down on a mat and place your elbows under your shoulders. Place your toes onto the mat and then push your forearms as you raise your body from the mat. Engage your abdominal muscles and try and form a straight line with your whole body. Keep your gaze down while taking steady, even breaths.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: ENOM
exercises.description: Compared to classic 4x4s, ENOMs (Every Minute On the Minute) may allow you to improve your anaerobic endurance for a longer sustained time.
howTo: Choose a moderate boulder and set a timer to 1 minute. Climb the boulder and rest for the remainder of the minute. At the start of the next minute, climb the boulder again. Do this for 4 to 10 minutes to complete a set and aim for 1-3 sets.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Boulder Mileage
exercises.description: A high volume bouldering session that should be performed on a boulder wall or steep board.
howTo: Aim to complete 20 boulders that will achieve the correct stimulus. You have an hour to attempt and complete all 20 boulders. That means you have roughly 3 minutes for each boulder. Attempt to flash every problem but you can have a second attempt, if you fail. Once the boulder has been completed or you failed a on your second attempt, you can rest for the remainder of the three minutes. You get the most out of this exercise if you are prepared to push yourself consistently.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Shoulder Rotations
exercises.description: Exercise to strengthen your shoulder.
howTo: Prone on a bench, engage your scapula and hold the dumbbell with your hand with your elbow out at 90 degrees from your body and with a 90 degree bend at the elbow.
Lower the weight down to the floor and then bring the weight back up to the starting position. This is one rep.
Focus on rotating from your shoulder rather than your elbow and maintain the 90 bend at the elbow throughout the whole movement.
Every repetition should be performed with good form, in full range of motion and in a controlled way.
Keep your scapula enfafed and don't allow winging in order to get a greater range of movement. Your range of movement may differ from the one in the images.

exercises.name: Contrast
exercises.description: Exercise to improve various aspects of your climbing.
howTo: Choose 8 boulders which should be semi-difficult for you. The boulders should not require any dynamic moves.
Climb each boulder 3 times. The first time as static as possible. The second time as dynamic as possible. And the third time should be an ideal blend of the static and dynamic attempts.
Be aware of your breathing as it should be in harmony with your climbing rythm and avoid holding your breath for longer periods.
Take a short rest between attempts and a longer rest between boulders.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Match
exercises.description: Exercise to improve your climbing technique and endurance.
howTo: Pick 4 semi difficult boulders and climb each 2-3 times.
While climbing, make sure to match each hold.
Take a 1 to 2 minute rest between repetitions and 5 minute rest between sets.

exercises.name: Tic Tac Toe
exercises.description: This exercise improves your body tension and your footwork. Depending on the holds you can also work your arms for endurance gains.
howTo: Pick 2 holds on a system wall which are about shoulder width apart and do not have an incut shape. You should be able to hang for about 20 seconds on those holds.
Hang on the holds and try to catch a hold with your left foot far down on your left side.
Return to the center and then catch a hold with your left foot on hip height of your left side.
Repeat this one more time with a hold overhead on left side.
Repeat the same on the right hand side with three holds on different levels. Once finished, you have done 1 rep.
Do 3-4 repetitions and two sets with a two minute rest between sets.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: Diagonal
exercises.description: Improve your body tension by hanging with only two limbs in steep terrain.
howTo: Pick a good hold directly at the edge of the roof.
Hang off the hold with both of your arms and pick a far away foot hold with your right foot.
Now let go off your right hand so you are effectively hanging off your left hand and your right foot.
Hold this position for 3-5 seconds
Switch foot and hand afterwards. This is one rep.
Do 5-8 reps for one set. Do two sets total with a 2 minute rest between.
exercises.info: You can vary the difficulty by difficulty by varying the distance of foothold and by hanging of straight arms or locking off.

exercises.name: One arm pull down with lock off
exercises.description: Improve your upper body strength with a one arm pull down and lock off.
howTo: On a cable machine, pull down with a single arm until your hand is on chest height.
From there, transition to a push down motion until your hand is on hip height.
Keep your arm in this position for three seconds.
Reverse the motion in a controlled manner. This is one repetition.
Do 8-10 reps for one arm to complete a set. Do the second set with the other arm.
exercises.info: You can vary the difficulty by difficulty by varying the distance of foothold and by hanging of straight arms or locking off.
